47:1: Surah Muhammad In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says: Those who disbelieve meaning in the verses of God and avert others from the way of God - He will render their deeds worthless meaning He will nullify and eliminate them and will not reward or recompense them, as God the Almighty says: And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make them as dust dispersed Then He the Almighty says: And those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning their hearts and souls believe and their limbs, inwardly and outwardly submit to God’s law and believe in what was revealed to Muhammad is a specific apposition to a general one and is evidence that it is a condition for the validity of faith after his mission, may God the Almighty say: And it is the truth from their Lord is a good parenthetical clause. That is why God the Almighty said: He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: meaning their situation. Mujahid said: their affair. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: their state, and all are similar. It was stated in the hadith about sneezing: May God guide you and set your affairs right. Then the Almighty said: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, meaning, We nullified the deeds of the disbelievers. We overlooked the misdeeds of the righteous and set their affairs right because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, meaning, they chose falsehood over the truth. “And because those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does God present to the people their examples,” meaning, He shows them the outcome of their deeds and what they will become in their afterlife. And God, the Almighty, knows best.

47:4: God Almighty says, guiding the believers to what they should rely on in their wars with the polytheists: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike at their necks meaning, when you confront them, then harvest them with swords until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them meaning, you have killed them completely then secure the bonds of the prisoners whom you capture. Then, after the war is over and the battle is over, you have a choice in your fate. If you wish, you can show them favor and release their prisoners for free, or if you wish, you can ransom them with money that you take from them and stipulate with them. It appears that this verse was revealed after the Battle of Badr, for God Almighty rebuked the believers for taking many prisoners on that day, in order to take ransom from them and reducing the killing on that day, saying: “It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land. You desire the goods of this world, but God desires the Hereafter. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.” Then Some scholars have claimed that this verse, which gives one the choice between ransoming a prisoner or showing mercy, was abrogated by the verse in which God the Almighty says: But when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Narrated by Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. This was also said by Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj. The others, who are the majority, said: It is not abrogated. Then some of them said: The imam only has the choice between showing mercy to the prisoner or ransoming him, and it is not permissible for him to kill him. Others said: Rather, he has the right to kill him if he wishes, based on the hadith in which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) killed An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt among the prisoners of Badr. Thumama ibn Aththal said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): What do you have, Thumama? He said: “If you kill, you will kill one who has committed a blood feud. If you show favor, you will show favor to one who is grateful. If you want money, then ask and you will be given whatever you wish.” Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, added: The imam has the choice between killing him, granting him favor, ransoming him, or enslaving him. This issue is explained in the science of branches of knowledge, and we have provided evidence for that in our book, Al-Ahkam. Praise and thanks be to God Almighty. And the words of God the Almighty: Until the war lays down its burdens. Mujahid said: Until Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, descends. It is as if he took it from the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: A group of my nation will continue to be victorious upon the truth until the last of them fights the Antichrist. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sulayman, from Al-Walid ibn Abd Al-Rahman Al-Jurashi, from Jubayr ibn Nufayl, who said: Salamah ibn Nufayl informed them that he came to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: I have let the horses go, laid down my weapons, and laid down the burdens of war, and I said: There is no fighting. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: "Now the fighting has come. A group of my nation will continue to be victorious over the people. God, the Almighty, will turn the hearts of some people astray, so they will fight them and God will provide for them through them until God's command comes and they are still in that state. Beware, the bond of the abode of the believers is in Ash-Sham, and goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection." And this is how Al-Nasa'i narrated it through two chains of narration on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayl, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nufayl Al-Sakuni. They said, There will be no fighting. He said, “They lied. Now the fighting has come. God the Almighty will continue to lift the hearts of people who fight them and provide for them from them until God’s command comes, and they are like that, and the heartland of the Muslims is in Ash-Sham.” This is how al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili narrated it on the authority of Dawud ibn Rashid. What is preserved is that it is from the narration of Salamah ibn Nufayl, as mentioned above. This strengthens the view that there is no abrogation, as if this ruling was legislated for war until there is no more war. Qatadah said, until the war lays down its burdens until there is no more polytheism, and this is like the statement of God the Almighty: And fight them until there is no more persecution and religion is for God alone. Then some of them said: Until the war lays down its burdens, meaning the burdens of the combatants, who are the polytheists, by repenting to God Almighty. It was said that it is the burdens of its people, by doing their utmost in obeying God Almighty. And the saying of God Almighty: "That is so. And if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them." That is, this. And if God had willed, We would not have taken revenge on the disbelievers with punishment and chastisement from Him. Rather, God the Almighty has left for you that which will distress you, and indeed, those whom you have counted are alive. Abu Sufyan said: One day is like the day of Badr, and war is a contest. But you will find an example that I did not command nor forbid. Then he went on to recite a rajaz poem and say: Exalted is Hubal, exalted is Hubal. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Say: ‘God is Most High and Most Majestic.’” Then Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Will you not answer him? They said: And what should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: “Say: ‘God is our Master, and you have no Master.’” Then the Almighty said: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning on the Day of Resurrection. And those who disbelieve will enjoy themselves and eat as livestock eat meaning in their worldly life, they will enjoy it and eat from it as livestock eat, gulping and biting, and they will have no concern except for that. For this reason, it is proven in the Sahih that the believer eats in one intestine, and the disbeliever eats in seven intestines. Then the Almighty said: And the Fire will be their abode meaning on the Day of their recompense. And the Almighty said: And how many a city was stronger in power than your city which expelled you meaning Mecca We destroyed them, so there was no helper for them This is a severe threat and a definite warning to the people of Mecca for their denial of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is the master of the messengers and the seal of the prophets. So if God, the Almighty, destroyed the nations who denied the messengers before him because of them, and they were stronger than these, then what do these people think God will do to them in this world and the next? If the punishment is lifted from many of them in this world due to the blessing of the presence of the Messenger, the Prophet of Mercy, then the punishment will be saved for those who disbelieve in him in their afterlife. “The punishment will be doubled for them. They were able to hear, and they were not able to see.” God the Almighty said: From your city which expelled you meaning those who expelled you from among them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father mentioned on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la on the authority of al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman on the authority of his father on the authority of Hanash on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both that when the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) left Mecca to the cave, he came to him. He said: He turned to Mecca and said: “You are the most beloved of God’s lands to God, and you are the most beloved of God’s lands to me. Had it not been that the polytheists expelled me, I would not have left you.” So the enemies were those who transgressed against God the Almighty in His sanctuary, or killed someone other than his killer, or killed during the days of ignorance. So God the Almighty revealed to His Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): And how many a city was stronger in power than your city which expelled you? We destroyed them, so none would have helped them.
47:14: God the Almighty says: Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord meaning, with insight and certainty of God’s command and religion, through what He has revealed in His Book of guidance and knowledge, and through what God has created in him of upright nature, like one to whom the evil of his deeds has been made pleasing, while they follow their own desires meaning this is not like that, as God the Almighty says: Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? And as God the Almighty says: “The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise - they are the successful ones.” Then God the Almighty says: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised Ikrimah said: The example of Paradise meaning its description in it are rivers of water unpolluted Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning unchanged. Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: unstinting. The Arabs say: water has become stagnant when its smell has changed. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: unstinting means pure and free of turbidity. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abdullah may God be pleased with him said: The rivers of Paradise gush forth from a mountain of musk. And rivers of milk of which the taste never changes. That is, it is extremely white, sweet, and creamy. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), It does not come from the udders of cattle. “And rivers of wine delicious to those who drink.” That is, it is not unpleasant in taste or smell like the wine of this world, which is pleasant in appearance, taste, smell, and action. Therein is no terror, nor do they suffer from headaches therefrom, nor are they intoxicated. “White, delicious to those who drink.” In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), It has not been squeezed by men with their feet. “And rivers of purified honey.” That is, it is extremely pure and has a pleasant color, taste, and smell. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), It does not come from the bellies of bees. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Harun told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Muawiyah, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: In Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of water, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine, and then rivers will burst forth from them after that. At-Tirmidhi narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashar, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Iyas al-Jariry, and he said: It is hasan sahih. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Asim told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Nu’man told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid Abu Qudamah Al-Ayadi told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These rivers gush forth from the Garden of Eden into a pit, and then they will burst forth into rivers after that. In the Sahih: “When you ask something of God, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise burst forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mus`ab bin Hamza al-Zubayri and Abdullah bin al-Safar al-Sakari told us: Ibrahim bin al-Mundhir al-Khuzami told us: Abd al-Rahman bin al-Mughira told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Ayyash told me on the authority of Dahlam bin al-Aswad. Dahlam said: My father al-Aswad also told me on the authority of Asim bin Laqeet, who said: Laqeet bin Amir went out as a delegate to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said: O Messenger of God, on what do we ascend from Paradise? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “On rivers of pure honey, and rivers of wine in which there is no headache or regret, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and water that does not turn stagnant, and fruits, by the life of your God, you know what is better than the like of it, and purified spouses.” I said: O Messenger of God, will the first of us in it be righteous spouses? He said: “Righteous women are for righteous men. You enjoy them as you enjoy yourself in this world, and they enjoy you, except that they do not give birth.” Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya said: Ya’qub bin Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, Al-Jariri told me, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: You may think that the rivers of Paradise flow in a furrow in the earth, but by God, they flow freely over the face of the earth, their edges are domes of pearls and their clay is the most fragrant musk. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Mahdi bin Hakim, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the saying of God the Almighty: And for them therein are all kinds of fruits is like His saying the Almighty: They will call therein for every kind of fruit, secure and His saying the Blessed and Exalted: In them are two kinds of every kind of fruit and His saying the Most High: And forgiveness from their Lord meaning with all of that. And His saying the Most High: Like one who will abide eternally in the Fire meaning, are those whose status in Paradise we mentioned like one who will abide eternally in the Fire? These are not like those, and the one who is in the degrees is not like the one who is in the depths. And they will be given to drink scalding water meaning, extremely hot, unbearably hot. So it will sever their intestines meaning, it will sever what is in their bellies of intestines and entrails - God forbid that.
47:15: He says: Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord meaning, with insight and certainty of the command of God and His religion, including His Book of guidance and knowledge, and thus God created him with the upright nature, like one whose evil deeds have been revealed to you and who follows their desires meaning this is not like that, like His statement: Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? And like His statement: The companions of the companions of Paradise are not equal to the companions of Paradise - all of them are the successful. Then Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The likeness of Paradise meaning its description in it are rivers untainted Ibn Radi Allahu Anhu, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning untainted. Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak and Ata' Al-Khurasani said: untainted. The Arabs say: tainted if its smell has changed. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: untainted means clear and free of turbidity. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, said: It is Paradise bursting forth from a mountain of musk. And rivers of milk the taste of which is unmatched. That is, it is extremely white, sweet, and delicious. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet, It does not come from the udders of game. “And rivers of wine delicious to those who drink.” That is, it is not unpleasant in taste or smell like the wine of this world, which is pleasant in appearance, taste, smell, and action. Therein is no terror, nor are they intoxicated by it. “They will not get a headache from it, nor will they get an intoxication.” White, delicious to those who drink. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet, It has not been squeezed by men with their feet. “And rivers of purified honey.” That is, it is extremely pure and has a pleasant color, taste, and smell. In a hadith attributed to the Prophet, It does not come from the bellies of elephants. Ahmad said: Zaid bin Harun told us, Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Al-Hakim bin Muawiyah, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: In Paradise there is a sea of milk, a sea of water, a sea of honey, and a sea of wine, then rivers will burst forth from them after that. At-Tirmidhi narrated it in Sifat Al-Jannah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashar Saeed, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Ibn Abias, on the authority of Al-Jariry, who said: It is good and authentic. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Asim told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Nu’man told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid Abu Qudamah Al-Ayadi told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These rivers gush forth from the Garden of Eden into a pit, then God will split forth rivers after that. And in it: If you sin, ask Him about Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and from it flows, that it is Paradise and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Aswad al-Tabarani said: Mus`ab bin Hamza al-Zubayri and `Abdullah bin Safar al-Sakri told us: Ibrahim bin al-Mundhir al-Khazami told us: `Abd al-Rahman bin al-Mughira told us: `Abd al-Rahman bin `Ayyash told me on the authority of Dahlam bin Qal Dahlam, on the authority of my father on the authority of `Asim bin Laqit, who said: Laqit bin `Amir went out as a delegate to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: O Messenger of God, are we present so that we may ascend from Paradise? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “It is like purified honey, and rivers of wine in which there is no headache or regret, and rivers of milk whose quality has not become stagnant, and water that has not turned stagnant, and fruits, by the life of your God, you know what you know, and better than its like, and wives that are abundant.” I said: O Messenger of God, will the first of us in it be healthy wives? He said: “Righteous women are for righteous men. You enjoy them as you enjoy them in this world, and they enjoy you, except that they do not give birth.” Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya said: Ya’qub bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, Al-Jariri told me, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: You may think that they are the rivers of Paradise flowing in a trench in the earth, but by God, they flow freely on the surface of the earth, without borders, like domes of pearls, and its clay is the most fragrant musk. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Mahdi bin Hakim, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And He said: And for them therein are all kinds of fruits, like the saying of the Almighty: Therein is a hand with every kind of fruit, secure, and His saying, the Blessed and Most High: In them are pairs of every kind of fruit, and His saying, the Most High: And forgiveness from their Lord, meaning with all of that. And the Almighty says: How many will abide eternally in the Fire, meaning those whose status in Paradise we mentioned, how many will abide eternally in the Fire? These are not as hot as those, and the one who is in the degrees is not like the one who is in the depths. And they will be given to drink the [severe] heat, meaning intense heat that cannot be endured. So He will cut off their intestines, meaning He will cut off what is in their stomachs of surplus and entrails—may God protect us from that.
47:16: He says, informing about the hypocrites in their country and their lack of understanding, as they used to sit with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and listen to his speech, but they did not understand anything from it and would leave him. They said to those who were given knowledge, from the Companions may God be pleased with them, What did he say just now? They did not understand what he said, nor did they care about it. God the Almighty said: Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed, and they follow their desires, meaning they have no correct understanding and no correct intention. Then God the Almighty said: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance, meaning they intended guidance, so God guided them to it, made them steadfast, and increased them in it. And gave them their righteousness, meaning He inspired them with their right path. And He said: Do they then take anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? That is, while they are heedless of it? Its portents have already come, That is, its signs, like the statement of the Most High: “This is a warner among the first warnings. The approaching hour has drawn near.” And like His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And His statement, may He be glorified and exalted: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it. And He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: Their reckoning has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness. So the mission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of the portents of the Hour, because he is the Seal of the Messengers through whom God completed and through whom He established the proof of the religion upon the worlds. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed us of the signs and portents of the Hour and explained them clearly in a way that no prophet before him was given, as is explained in detail in its place. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The mission of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is one of the portents of the Hour, and it is as he said. That is why it is mentioned among his names (peace and blessings be upon him) that he is the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Epic Battle, the Gatherer who will gather mankind at his feet, and the Last One after whom there will be no prophet. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Fadhi ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, Sahl ibn Sa’d may God be pleased with him said: I saw the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) pointing with his two fingers like this, with the middle finger and the one on which he had written: I and the Hour have been sent like these two. Then the first finger said: How can they, when their reminder reaches them, benefit them? How can the disbelievers be reminded if that distracts them? It will not benefit them, like His saying: Then the Day of Man, that I will be for him a Friday. “And they will say, ‘We believe in it.’ But how can they approach it from a distant place?” And God the Almighty said: And tell them that there is no god but God. This means that there is no god but God can be a command with knowledge of that, and for this reason God the Almighty followed it with: And ask forgiveness for Your sin and for the believing men and the believing women. And in a Sahih: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “O God, forgive me my sin, my ignorance, and my excess in my affairs, for You know them better than I. O God, forgive me my lapses, my seriousness, my mistakes, my intentions, and all of that.” It is true that he used to say at the end of the prayer: “O God, forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I have left behind, what I have kept secret and what I have been drunk with, and what I have done in excess. You know it better than I do. You are my God and there is no god but You.” And it is true that he said: O people, repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him more than seventy times a day. Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Sarjis say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and I ate from his food. I said: May God forgive you, O Messenger of God. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And for you. I said: I seek forgiveness for you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, and for you. He recited: And seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. Then he looked to some of it, to the right - or his left shoulder, Shu`bah, who was uncertain - independently, like the plural form of warts. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Jarir Abu Hatim, through various chains of transmission on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal. In the other hadith, Abu Ya`la narrated it: Muhammad ibn `Awn told us, `Uthman ibn Matar told us, `Abd al-Ghafur told us, on the authority of Ubayrah, on the authority of Abu... It was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “You must adhere to ‘La ilaha illa God’ and to seeking forgiveness, so increase them in them, for Satan said: ‘I was destroyed by sins, and they destroyed me by ‘La ilaha illa God’ and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that, I destroyed them with desires, for they think that they are guided.’” And in the narrated hadith: “Satan said: ‘By Your glory and majesty, I will continue to mislead them as long as their beginnings in their corruption die.’ God the Almighty said: ‘By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as I seek forgiveness.’” There are many hadiths about the virtue of Ghaffar. God the Most High said: And God knows your movement and your resting place, meaning He knows you during your day and your resting place during your night, like His saying: Who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day, and His saying, the Most High: “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a register.” Juraij, and this is an option. Ibn Jarir, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Your movements in this world and your abode in the Hereafter. And he said: Your movements in this world and your abode in your graves, and the first and most evident, and God knows best.
47:17: God the Almighty says, informing us about the hypocrites and their dullness and lack of understanding. They used to sit with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and listen to his speech, but they did not understand anything of it. When they left him, they said to those who had been given knowledge, from the Companions may God be pleased with them, What did he say just now? They did not understand what he said, nor did they care about it. God the Almighty says: Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed, and they follow their desires, meaning they have no correct understanding and no correct intention. Then the Almighty says: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance, meaning those who intended guidance, God the Almighty guided them to it, guided them to it, made them steadfast in it, and increased them in it. And gave them their righteousness, meaning He inspired them with their right path. And the Almighty’s saying: Do they then await anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly? That is, while they are heedless of it? But already its portents have come. That is, the signs of its approach, like His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: “This is a warner among the first warnings. The approaching hour has drawn near.” And His saying, the Majestic and Sublime: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And His saying, the Exalted and Sublime: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it. And His saying, the Exalted and Sublime: The account of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. So the sending of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of the portents of the Hour, because he is the Seal of the Messengers through whom God, the Exalted, completed the religion and established the proof against the worlds. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed us of the signs and portents of the Hour, and he explained them and clarified them in a way that no prophet before him was given, as is explained in detail in its place. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The mission of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is one of the portents of the Hour, and it is as he said. That is why it is mentioned among his names (peace and blessings be upon him) that he is the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Epic Battle, the Gatherer who will gather mankind at his feet, and the Last One after whom there will be no prophet. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Fadil ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, Sahl ibn Sa'd may God be pleased with him narrated to us, he said: I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) pointing with his two fingers like this, with the middle finger and the one next to it: I and the Hour have been sent like these two. Then God the Almighty said: Then how will they, when their reminder comes to them, be reminded? That is, how will the disbelievers be reminded when the Resurrection comes to them when it will not benefit them, as God the Almighty said: On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder come to him? "And they will say, 'We believe in it,' but how can they approach it from a distant place?" And God the Almighty said: "So know that there is no god but God." This is information that there is no god but God, and it is not possible for Him to command knowledge of that, and for this reason He followed it with His saying: "And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women." In the Sahih: It is narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "O God, forgive me my sin, my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and that which You know better than I. O God, forgive my jesting and my seriousness, my mistakes and my deliberate actions, and all of that is with me." In Sahih it is reported that he used to say at the end of the prayer: “O God, forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I will do in the future, what I have kept secret and what I have declared, and what I have done in excess, and what You know better than I. You are my God, there is no god but You.” In Sahih it is reported that he said: O people, repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him more than seventy times a day. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Sarjis say: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ate some of his food. I said: May God forgive you, O Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And for you. I said: I seek forgiveness for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, and for you too. He recited: And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. Then I looked at part of his right shoulder - or his left shoulder, Shu’bah, who was unsure - and saw that it was like a group with warts on it. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal. In the other hadith narrated by Abu Ya’la: Muhammad ibn ‘Awn told us, ‘Uthman ibn Matar told us, ‘Abd al-Ghafur told us, on the authority of Abu Nusayrah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “You must say ‘There is no god but God’ and seek forgiveness, and do them often, for Satan said: ‘I have destroyed people with sins, and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” In the reported hadith: “Satan said: ‘By Your glory and majesty, I will continue to mislead them as long as their souls are in their bodies.’ So God, the Almighty, said: ‘By My glory and majesty.’” I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness. There are many hadiths about the virtue of seeking forgiveness. God the Most High said: And God knows your movements and your resting place. That is, He knows your actions during the day and your resting place at night, as He the Most High said: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. And He the Most High said: “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.” This is the opinion of Ibn Jurayj and it is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that it was your movements in this world and your resting place in the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: Your movements in this world and your resting place in your graves. The first is more appropriate and clearer, and God knows best.

47:19: God the Almighty says, informing us about the hypocrites and their dullness and lack of understanding. They used to sit with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and listen to his speech, but they did not understand anything of it. When they left him, they said to those who had been given knowledge, from the Companions may God be pleased with them, What did he say just now? They did not understand what he said, nor did they care about it. God the Almighty says: Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed, and they follow their desires, meaning they have no correct understanding and no correct intention. Then the Almighty says: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance, meaning those who intended guidance, God the Almighty guided them to it, guided them to it, made them steadfast in it, and increased them in it. And gave them their righteousness, meaning He inspired them with their right path. And the Almighty’s saying: Do they then await anything but that the Hour should come upon them suddenly? That is, while they are heedless of it? But already its portents have come. That is, the signs of its approach, like His saying, the Blessed and Exalted: “This is a warner among the first warnings. The approaching hour has drawn near.” And His saying, the Majestic and Sublime: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And His saying, the Exalted and Sublime: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it. And His saying, the Exalted and Sublime: The account of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. So the sending of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of the portents of the Hour, because he is the Seal of the Messengers through whom God, the Exalted, completed the religion and established the proof against the worlds. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) informed us of the signs and portents of the Hour, and he explained them and clarified them in a way that no prophet before him was given, as is explained in detail in its place. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The mission of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is one of the portents of the Hour, and it is as he said. That is why it is mentioned among his names (peace and blessings be upon him) that he is the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Epic Battle, the Gatherer who will gather mankind at his feet, and the Last One after whom there will be no prophet. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Fadil ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, Sahl ibn Sa'd may God be pleased with him narrated to us, he said: I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) pointing with his two fingers like this, with the middle finger and the one next to it: I and the Hour have been sent like these two. Then God the Almighty said: Then how will they, when their reminder comes to them, be reminded? That is, how will the disbelievers be reminded when the Resurrection comes to them when it will not benefit them, as God the Almighty said: On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder come to him? "And they will say, 'We believe in it,' but how can they approach it from a distant place?" And God the Almighty said: "So know that there is no god but God." This is information that there is no god but God, and it is not possible for Him to command knowledge of that, and for this reason He followed it with His saying: "And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women." In the Sahih: It is narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "O God, forgive me my sin, my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and that which You know better than I. O God, forgive my jesting and my seriousness, my mistakes and my deliberate actions, and all of that is with me." In Sahih it is reported that he used to say at the end of the prayer: “O God, forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I will do in the future, what I have kept secret and what I have declared, and what I have done in excess, and what You know better than I. You are my God, there is no god but You.” In Sahih it is reported that he said: O people, repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him more than seventy times a day. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn Sarjis say: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ate some of his food. I said: May God forgive you, O Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And for you. I said: I seek forgiveness for you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, and for you too. He recited: And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. Then I looked at part of his right shoulder - or his left shoulder, Shu’bah, who was unsure - and saw that it was like a group with warts on it. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal. In the other hadith narrated by Abu Ya’la: Muhammad ibn ‘Awn told us, ‘Uthman ibn Matar told us, ‘Abd al-Ghafur told us, on the authority of Abu Nusayrah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “You must say ‘There is no god but God’ and seek forgiveness, and do them often, for Satan said: ‘I have destroyed people with sins, and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” In the reported hadith: “Satan said: ‘By Your glory and majesty, I will continue to mislead them as long as their souls are in their bodies.’ So God, the Almighty, said: ‘By My glory and majesty.’” I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness. There are many hadiths about the virtue of seeking forgiveness. God the Most High said: And God knows your movements and your resting place. That is, He knows your actions during the day and your resting place at night, as He the Most High said: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day. And He the Most High said: “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.” This is the opinion of Ibn Jurayj and it is the preferred opinion of Ibn Jarir. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that it was your movements in this world and your resting place in the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: Your movements in this world and your resting place in your graves. The first is more appropriate and clearer, and God knows best.
47:20: God Almighty says, informing about the believers that they wished for the legitimacy of jihad, but when God Almighty imposed it and commanded it, many people turned away from it, as He, the Blessed and Exalted, says: “Have you not seen those to whom it was said, ‘Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah?’ But when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party of them feared the people as they fear God or even more, and they said, ‘Our Lord, why did You decree fighting upon us? Why did You not delay us for a short term?’ Say, ‘The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears God, and you will not be wronged a thread.’” And God Almighty says here: And those who believe say, ‘Why was a surah not sent down?’ That is, one that includes the ruling on fighting. For this reason, He said: But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one fainting from death, That is, from their fear, terror, and cowardice in meeting the enemies. Then He says, encouraging them, It is more appropriate for them * to obey and speak graciously, That is, it would have been more appropriate for them to listen and obey, that is, in the current situation. So when the matter is decided, That is, The situation became serious, and the battle was present. If they had been true to God, that is, if they had been sincere in their intentions toward Him, it would have been better for them. And the Almighty said: Then, if you turn away meaning from jihad and refrain from it, will you then cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship? meaning, will you return to the ignorant ignorance you were doing, shedding blood and severing ties of kinship? For this reason, the Almighty said: Those are the ones whom God has cursed and made deaf and blinded their sight. This is a prohibition against corruption on earth in general, and against severing ties of kinship in particular. Indeed, God the Almighty has commanded reform on earth and maintaining ties of kinship, which is being kind to relatives in word and deed and spending money. Authentic and good hadiths have been transmitted on this from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) through many chains of transmission and many aspects. Al-Bukhari said: Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, Sulayman told us, Muawiyah bin Abi Mazrad told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who said: “God the Almighty created creation, and when He finished, the womb stood up and seized the waist of the Most Merciful, the Almighty, and He said, ‘Easy! ’ It said, ‘This is the place of one who seeks refuge in You from severing ties of kinship. ’ So the Almighty said: Would you not be pleased that I should connect with those who connect with you and sever with those who sever with you? She said: Yes. He said: Then that is yours. Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said: “Recite, if you wish, ‘Would you then, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?’” Then Al-Bukhari narrated it through two other chains of narration on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Mizrad, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Recite, if you wish, ‘Would you then, if you were given authority, cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?’ Muslim narrated it on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Abi Mizrad. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, Uyaynah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Jushan narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: There is no sin for which God is more likely to hasten its punishment in this world, along with what He has in store for its perpetrator in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing family ties. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ismail i.e., Ibn Ulayyah. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sahih hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Ma’ri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn ‘Ibad al-Makhzumi narrated to us, on the authority of Thawban may God be pleased with him, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever is pleased with a postponement of life or an increase in provision, let him uphold the ties of kinship. Ahmad alone narrated it and it has a corroborating evidence in Sahih al-Bukhari. Ahmad also said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hajjaj ibn Artah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, I have relatives whom I maintain ties of kinship with, but they sever them, I pardon, but they wrong me, I do good, but they do evil. Should I reward them? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “No, then you will all be left alone, but strive to be kind to them and maintain ties of kinship with them, for there will continue to be a supporter with you from God, the Almighty, as long as you are like that.” Ahmad alone transmitted this from this chain of narration, and it has a corroborating evidence from another chain of narration. Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la told us, Fitr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The womb is suspended from the Throne, and the one who maintains ties of kinship is not the one who reciprocates, but the one who maintains ties of kinship is the one who, when his ties of kinship are severed, maintains them.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Ahmad said: Buhaiz told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Abu Thamamah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The womb will be placed on the Day of Resurrection with a branch like the branch of a spindle. It will speak with a fluent, smooth tongue. It will sever whoever severs it and restore whoever restores it.” Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Qabus, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr may God be pleased with them both, conveying it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “The merciful will be shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth and the people of the heavens will have mercy upon you. The womb is a branch of the Most Merciful. Whoever maintains it will maintain it and whoever severs it will sever it.” Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, and this is what is narrated with a chain of transmission of priority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hisham al-Dastawai told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Qarith, that his father told him that he entered upon Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf may God be pleased with him while he was sick. Abd al-Rahman may God be pleased with him said to him, “Uphold your ties of kinship, for the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, ‘God, the Almighty, said, “I am the Most Gracious. I created the womb and derived its name from My name. So whoever upholds it, I will uphold it, and whoever severs it, I will sever him. And whoever severs it, I will destroy him.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this chain of narration. Ahmad also narrated it from the hadith of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of al-Raddad or Abu al-Raddad, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, on his authority. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the narration of Abu Salamah, on the authority of his father. There are many hadiths on this subject. Al-Tabarani said: Ali bin Abdul Aziz told us, Muhammad bin Ammar Al-Mawsili told us, Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Farafisa, on the authority of Abu Omar Al-Basri, on the authority of Sulayman, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Souls are like conscripted soldiers. Those that recognize each other will get along, and those that do not will differ.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the same: “When speech becomes public, deeds become hidden, tongues become unified, hearts hate each other, and every relative severs his kinship, then at that time God will curse them, deafen them, and blind their sight.” And there are many hadiths on this, and God knows best.
